heading: 3-Day Nanjing Itinerary for First-Time Visitors (2026)
description: Plan three days in Nanjing with Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum, Ming Xiaoling, Nanjing Museum, the Memorial Hall, Qinhuai River, city walls and train tips.
quickAnswer: For three full days in Nanjing, reserve one day for the wooded Zhongshan scenic area and Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum, one for the city centre, a major museum and a thoughtful visit to the Nanjing Massacre Memorial Hall, and one for the old city walls and Qinhuai River area. The memorial is a solemn historical site, not a quick photo stop; allow time and follow its visitor rules. Check each venue's current reservation and closure policy, and verify whether your train uses Nanjing or Nanjing South station.

contentSections.title: Three days at a glance

rows: Day 1
Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum and one other Zhongshan scenic-area site
Keep the large eastern park area together
Day 2
Nanjing Museum or Presidential Palace, then Nanjing Massacre Memorial Hall
Leave space for history and reflection
Day 3
City wall or Zhonghua Gate, Confucius Temple and Qinhuai River
Explore the southern old-city area

items: This assumes three complete sightseeing days, with arrival and departure time counted separately.
The Zhongshan area and the southern old city are not adjacent. Avoid crossing the city several times each day.
The museum, memorial and mausoleum have different entry systems and opening days. Check each site individually before booking transport around it.

contentSections.title: Day 1: the Zhongshan scenic area
items: Begin with Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum after checking the current reservation method, opening day, identity-document rules and permitted entry time.
Be ready for stairs and a long outdoor walk. If mobility or weather makes the climb unsuitable, spend more time at an accessible area of the larger scenic district instead.
Choose only one substantial second stop, such as Ming Xiaoling or another museum or site in the Zhongshan area. Confirm its separate ticket and the distance between entrances.

Ming Xiaoling is part of the UNESCO-listed Imperial Tombs of the Ming and Qing Dynasties. Read its historical context before visiting and allow time for the tree-lined approach rather than racing through a gate.
Return to the city for dinner; do not assume you can fit a full Qinhuai evening and two extensive eastern sites into one relaxed day.

contentSections.title: Day 2: museum and remembrance
items: Choose Nanjing Museum for a broad introduction to regional history, or the Presidential Palace for a different focus. Check the exact venue, current reservation channel, accepted ID and exhibition access.
Leave a proper midday break before the Memorial Hall of the Victims in Nanjing Massacre by Japanese Invaders. Its exhibitions cover traumatic events and deserve time and respectful attention.

The memorial's official visitor guide lists advance reservation information and accepts passports among its valid identity documents. Recheck the official guide for your date; do not assume walk-in admission.
Keep the rest of the day light. If you prefer not to visit the memorial, use this block for a second museum or a quieter neighbourhood without implying the sites are interchangeable.
Allow travel time between the city-centre museum options and the memorial. End near your hotel rather than scheduling an unrelated distant attraction.

contentSections.title: Day 3: walls, southern lanes and Qinhuai
items: Explore one accessible section of Nanjing's city wall or Zhonghua Gate after checking the specific entry point and ticket rules. The walls are long; choose a segment rather than planning a complete circuit.
Move through the southern old-city area toward the Confucius Temple district, noticing side streets and local food rather than staying only on the busiest shopping frontage.
Walk by the Qinhuai River in daylight or early evening. Boat trips are optional and may use different piers, routes and seasonal times; check the actual departure point before paying.
For a late train, leave this day flexible, retrieve luggage and calculate the trip to your exact railway station with a security buffer.

contentSections.title: Where to stay and how to arrive
items: Stay near a useful Metro interchange in the central city if you want balanced access to Zhongshan, museums and Qinhuai. A hotel in the Qinhuai area favours evening walks but may involve a longer eastern-area transfer.
Nanjing and Nanjing South are different railway stations. Check the station printed on your ticket; Shanghai also has multiple departure stations.

Use China Railway 12306 to check your actual train and enter your passport details exactly as required. The official railway FAQ confirms that foreign passengers can use valid passports for real-name tickets.
If arriving by air, check the current airport-to-city Metro or road route and your hotel's late check-in arrangements. Save the Chinese hotel name and address offline.
Do not pick accommodation solely because it claims to be near a named attraction; verify the nearest station, entrance and realistic travel time.

items: Summer heat, rain and peak holiday crowds can make outdoor walking much slower. Start early where allowed and keep a museum or rest break.
Avoid relying on old blog prices or screenshots for tickets. Official notices and your live booking confirmation take priority.

contentSections.title: Adapt the route to your interests
items: With one day, choose either Zhongshan's mausoleum area or the museum and southern old city. Adding the memorial should be a deliberate decision with enough time.
With two days, keep Zhongshan on one day and a museum, the memorial and Qinhuai on the other, trimming the list if admission times conflict.
For families or limited mobility, reduce stairs and walking, choose one major site per half-day and confirm accessible entry and transport.

If museums matter most, give the Nanjing Museum a generous block and move the Presidential Palace to another day or another visit. If food and neighbourhoods matter most, spend more of Day 3 beyond the busiest Qinhuai frontage.

faqs: Are three days enough for Nanjing?
Yes for one Zhongshan day, one museum and remembrance day, and one old-city and Qinhuai day. Allow more time for several museums or distant excursions.
Which railway station should I use in Nanjing?
Use the exact station on your ticket. Nanjing and Nanjing South are different stations and require different transfers.
Do I need to reserve Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum?
Check the current official scenic-area entry and reservation instructions for your date, including opening days and acceptable identity documents.
Can foreigners visit the Nanjing Massacre Memorial Hall?
The memorial's official visitor guide lists passports among valid documents. Check the current reservation channel and visiting rules before going, and allow an unhurried, respectful visit.
Can I visit Ming Xiaoling and Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum on the same day?
Often yes with an early start and suitable entry arrangements, but both involve walking and may have different tickets. Choose only those two main sites for a manageable Zhongshan day.
Can ChinaEase Buddy customise the three days?
Yes. Share your arrival station, dates, hotel, mobility, museum interests and memorial preference so the route fits your actual visit.
